claims.why: All accounts went from $676,995.82 to $754,350.31: +$77,354.49, +11.4%, not 18%. The balance ($754K) is right; the percentage is not.

claims.quote: Fuel rose ~$19.5K (about 12%) on higher diesel prices and the extra Winnipeg miles.
claims.why: Fuel went from $167,589.04 to $187,098.65: +$19,509.61, +11.6%. US fleet-card fuel rose $14,270.18 (daily spend up about 5% on price and miles) and Manitoba fuel billed in CAD rose $5,239.43 (eight Brandon MB fills against five, at a stronger CAD). Price and volume leave no single transaction.
claims.share_note: A price-and-volume cause spread over 74 fuel lines; the Manitoba lines carry the 'Winnipeg miles' part as CAD conversions.

claims.quote: Driver wages were up 6% on the higher mileage.
claims.why: Driver wages went from $182,457.81 to $193,547.53: +$11,089.72, +6.1%. Drivers are paid by the mile; both semi-monthly settlements rose about 6%.
claims.share_note: A rate-times-volume cause across the two settlement lines.

claims.quote: Purchased transportation was up 25%, or about $40K, as we brokered out the peak overflow on the Harlow Foods account.
claims.why: Purchased transportation went from $149,511.34 to $177,400.00: +$27,888.66, +18.7%. Both stated figures are too high ($40K is 43% over; 25% against 18.7%).

claims.quote: Maintenance came in about $11K lower: September carried the in-frame overhaul on unit 2207, partly offset by this month's DPF cleaning program.
claims.why: Maintenance went from $28,156.23 to $17,162.42: -$10,993.81. September's in-frame overhaul ($18,500) did not recur and October's DPF cleaning ($6,600) is new: net -$11,900, 108% of the change.

claims.quote: Tires were up about $10K on the winter steer-tire program (14 tractors).
claims.why: Tires went from $2,800.00 to $12,840.00: +$10,040.00. 'Steer tire replacement - 14 tractors (winter program)' is $9,940, 99%.

claims.quote: Dispatch software was up $3.3K with the trailer trackers going live.
claims.why: Dispatch & ELD software went from $3,930.00 to $4,000.00: +$70.00. The trailer trackers ($3,300, TrackPoint Telematics) are booked to Equipment Leases, which rose exactly $3,300.

claims.quote: Insurance increased $5.6K, all of it the October 1 renewal of the auto liability and cargo program.
claims.why: Insurance went from $38,100.00 to $43,700.00: +$5,600.00. The monthly prepaid amortisation for auto liability and cargo went from $31,200 (2025 policy) to $36,800 (renewal 10/1/26): 100%.

claims.quote: Cargo claims rose $12.4K on the Harlow Foods water damage claim.
claims.why: Cargo claims went from $600.00 to $3,000.00: +$2,400.00. The Harlow Foods claim ($12,400) was largely recovered from the cargo underwriter in the same month (-$9,400): net $3,000, the deductible. The sentence quotes the gross claim as the variance.

claims.quote: Driver recruiting rose $7.6K on the expanded job-board campaign.
claims.why: Driver recruiting went from $1,600.00 to $9,200.00: +$7,600.00, so the amount is right. The job-board campaign rose $2,900 (38%); the larger part is CDL school tuition reimbursement for two hires ($4,700).

claims.quote: Tolls and permits were flat at about $9K.
claims.why: Tolls & permits went from $9,060.00 to $9,200.00: +$140.00 (+1.5%), flat in any reading, at about $9K.

non_claims.quote: Loaded miles were up 6.4% to 1.21M, revenue per loaded mile held at $2.71, and the operating ratio improved to 93.8%.
